messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-prod-3 saturating — queue growth + sustained throttling detected for model:v33. Metrics crossing thresholds (gpu_util>95%, queue_len>120) at 5012345678

deploy-bot: just triggered: rollout v33 -> prod (canary->full) at 5012345600 — large-context path enabled (ctx_limit=8192). Rolling update completed ~10m ago.

alicia: oncall here, paging in. seeing steady queue growth on pool-3, token throughput spike correlates with v33 traffic. prefills up ~3x baseline.

rafael: confirmed. KV cache warmup on v33 is causing higher memory working set and longer prefill times. autoscaler logs show "scale_up_request rejected: quota limit reached" for pool-3.

sam: customer impact? any 5xx/429s?

mia: CS telemetry: a subset of enterprise customers hitting higher latency, several alerts for 429s on routes pinned to v33. Percent of requests throttled ~4.8% last 5m. Not yet widespread but bumping SLA pages.

jon: stack traces from the runtime show backlog when prefill tasks block execution threads, e.g.:
```
W/Runtime: prefill_task_timeout for request=abcd1234 ctx=6000ms
E/Autoscaler: scale_up_request failed: no_more_pools_available
```

alicia: autoscaler reached max_pools (configured hard limit). We can't spin up more dedicated GPUs in this account/region. That explains rejected scale requests.

ops-bot: note: cold-gpu-pool has 0 spare nodes (all reserved). vendor quota check shows no free capacity in region-us-east-1.

rafael: quick options: 1) rollback v33 -> v32 (instant reduce ctx blowup), 2) enable adaptive token cutoff for v33 (limit ctx to 4096), 3) emergency scale override (requires infra approval and vendor quota), 4) route some traffic to fallback smaller model.

alicia: doing risk assessment. Rollback safest and fastest. What's deploy rollback ETA?

deploy-bot: rollback window open. `rdw deploy rollback --service model-v33 --to v32` will start canary at 5012345730 and finish ~3m if no blocking hooks.

sam: let's prepare roll forward mitigations in case rollback fails. Rafael, can you enable an ingress throttle for non-enterprise routes to reduce pressure?

rafael: yes — applying rate-limit rule to route group `public-text-gen` to 60r/s from 200r/s. Pushing now.

raff: (typo) meant to say applying now.

rafael: rate-limit applied. observable: queue length stabilized and dropped ~20% in 60s. latency still elevated but trending down.

mia: FYI customer comms draft: "We're investigating higher latency and throttling affecting text generation for some customers following a model update. We're rolling back the update and will share an ETA shortly." Approve?

sam: approve. Send to affected customers list tomorrow unless we can provide immediate fix.

alicia: starting rollback now. monitor dashboards and autoscaler logs for 3m.

deploy-bot: rollback started at 5012345730. Canary on 2 nodes. healthhooks OK.

jon: watching logs: prefill rates dropping quickly on canary nodes. total queue_len down 45% after canary promotion.

ops-bot: autoscaler accepted subsequent scale requests; previous "quota reached" errors not appearing — seems rollback dropped memory pressure enabling normal scaling.

alicia: rollback complete at 5012345775. v32 now active. Immediate metrics: gpu_util back to ~70%, queue_len down to baseline. Latency trending toward normal.

mia: CS: throttles down to 0.9% from 4.8%. Sending update to customers: rollback completed, monitoring.

sam: great. Next steps for RCA and follow-up: Rafael/Research to investigate v33 warmup behavior and KV eviction thresholds; Eng-runtime to add pre-deploy load simulation for large-context variants; Product to decide whether v33 feature flags (context cap) should be gradual by default.

rafael: noted. Immediate postmortem items I'm adding: reproduce prefill amplification in staging with traffic generator, capture per-request prefills and KV hit rates, verify autoscaler handles transient spikes without hard quota rejections (or at least fail open to fallback pool).

alicia: ops action items: temporarily increase max_pools soft limit for region-us-east-1 in config to avoid hitting hard cap during rollouts. Will file infra change request; may need vendor quota increase.

jon: create a follow-up runbook entry for "large-context rollout checklist" — include canary-size, slow-roll %, circuit-breaker rules (eg. automatic rollback if queue_len > 100 for 5m), and autoscaler override playbook.

mia: scheduling customer bridge if customers still see issues; for now CS will hold until morning follow-ups.

sam: handoff: I'm oncall until 0700PT; alicia please take bridging lead for any late regressions, Rafael you'll own the engineering RCA. Tagging @tom-infra for vendor quota follow-up.

alicia: taking lead. I'll keep an eye and escalate if any regression. adding notes to the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/5012345678

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: primary symptom mitigated (rollback completed). Postmortem assigned. Severity: Sev2 -> follow-up.

rafael: quick log excerpt for postmortem: 
```
Timeline:
- 5012345600: v33 rollout complete
- 5012345670: prefills spike detected
- 5012345690: autoscaler rejected scale_up (quota)
- 5012345730: rollback initiated
- 5012345775: rollback complete, metrics recovering
```

alicia: adding customer impact summary: ~4.8% throttled requests over 12m window, elevated p50/p95 latency for 18m, no data loss. Customers affected: 5 enterprise tenants with pinned routes.

sam: thanks team. We'll do a deeper RCA and follow up with timeline and mitigation plan in the postmortem doc. Handoff complete.

mia: I'll draft the customer incident note once RCA has initial findings.

jon: leaving a TODO to add an automated pre-deploy load check into CI so context-expanding flags run a synthetic prefill scenario.

alicia: logging done. closing thread but will append postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
